newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crude prices drift lower, grades stay weaker.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crude prices drift lower, grades stay weaker.

text.p: U.S. crude prices drifted lower Thursday, ending weaker on technical sentiment the market is overbought, while domestic grades maintained weaker prices established in the morning.
Crude futures ended weaker due to fears gasoline stocks are oversupplied, settling at $23.54 a barrel a day ahead of expiration for the October contract.
Grades were weakened by fundamentally well-supplied markets, and refiners looking to fish deals at low ranges.
Oct West Texas Intermediate/Cushing ended at $23.40-50, down 30-40 cts from the closing levels Wednesday.
Grade values improved from the lowest ranges seen in the afternoon, but were still some 10-20 cts lower for sweet grades from the trades confirmed on Wednesday.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James done at flat to the WTI/Cushing, up from negative levels earlier in the day.
Midland/WTI was last done at 4 cts under the WTI/Cushing, and Heavy Louisiana Sweet was talked at 45-40 cts under WTI.
Sour grades were done late at minus $1.30 for Eugene Island, 15 cts firmer than earlier deals at minus $1.45.
West Texas Sour/Midland was traded last at a $1.33 discount to the WTI, in-line with previous trading levels.
Oct Postings-Plus was steady at around $2.05-$2.10.

Crude brokers said there was pressure on the domestic grades from a variety of factors. One source said the improving arbitrage could see flows of West African and North Sea parcels accelerate in the near-term.

Additionally, the extremely weak gasoline crack spreads have depressed interest from refiners. Some players wondered if planned refinery turnarounds at major plants were being pushed up from October and November dates.
"Margins are getting pummeled, people are looking for other feed stocks," said an oil trader.
Major turnarounds were seen for the Amerada Hess refinery in St. Croix in the U.S. Virgin Islands for late October, and at the Sun Co Philadelphia refinery, also in October.
Both companies said the dates for the maintenance and improvement programs were not changed.

Reports the United States moved a second aircraft carrier into the Gulf and sent more troops to Kuwait on Thursday as part of military build-up to deter Iraq, failed to move the market, traders noted.
In the U.S. aftermarket, Brent paper was traded sparingly, with only partial deals seen for November Brent at $21.83 and $21.80. Spreads were done for Oct/Nov at plus 48 cts twice.
